queue.description:
# Fix and extend pagination
`paginate.py` backs the list pages of the site. Support reported this:
> With 20 items and 10 per page, the site shows a third, empty page.
## What to change
1. `page_count(total_items, per_page)` is the number of pages needed: 20 items at 10 per page is 2 pages, 21 items is 3. Zero items is 1 page, because the site always shows one page.
2. `page_slice(total_items, per_page, page)` returns `(start, end)`, the indexes of the first item on the page and one past the last, so that `items[start:end]` is the page. Pages are numbered from 1. The last page may be short. A page below 1 or above `page_count` raises `ValueError`.
3. `page_window(total_items, per_page, page, size=5)` returns the list of page numbers to show in the pager. Its rules:
   - It lists `size` consecutive page numbers, or all pages when there are fewer than `size`.
   - The current page is in the middle when it can be. With an even `size` the extra page goes after the current one: `size=4` around page 5 of 10 is `[4, 5, 6, 7]`.
   - Near the first or the last page the window is shifted to stay inside 1 to `page_count`, and it keeps its full length: page 10 of 10 with `size=5` is `[6, 7, 8, 9, 10]`.
   - A page below 1 or above `page_count`, and a `size` below 1, raise `ValueError`.
4. In all three functions `per_page` below 1 and `total_items` below 0 raise `ValueError`.
Run the provided tests with `python3 -m unittest test_visible -v`.
Acceptance criteria
Every rule in the description is implemented in paginate.py

The provided tests in test_visible.py pass, with that file unchanged

solution.name: paginate.py
solution.text:
"""Page arithmetic for list pages."""


def _validate(total_items, per_page):
    if total_items < 0:
        raise ValueError("total_items must be non-negative")
    if per_page < 1:
        raise ValueError("per_page must be at least 1")


def page_count(total_items, per_page):
    """Number of pages needed for the items.

    20 items at 10 per page is 2 pages, 21 items is 3.
    Zero items is 1 page (the site always shows one page).
    """
    _validate(total_items, per_page)
    if total_items == 0:
        return 1
    return (total_items + per_page - 1) // per_page


def page_slice(total_items, per_page, page):
    """(start, end) indexes of the items on a page. Pages are numbered from 1.

    The last page may be short, so ``end`` never exceeds ``total_items``.
    A page below 1 or above ``page_count`` raises ``ValueError``.
    """
    _validate(total_items, per_page)
    pages = page_count(total_items, per_page)
    if page < 1 or page > pages:
        raise ValueError("no such page")
    start = (page - 1) * per_page
    end = min(start + per_page, total_items)
    return start, end


def page_window(total_items, per_page, page, size=5):
    """Page numbers to show in the pager, centred on the current page.

    Lists ``size`` consecutive page numbers, or all pages when there are
    fewer than ``size``. The current page sits in the middle when it can;
    with an even ``size`` the extra page goes after the current page, so
    ``size=4`` around page 5 of 10 is ``[4, 5, 6, 7]``. Near the ends the
    window is shifted to stay within 1..page_count while keeping its full
    length, so page 10 of 10 with ``size=5`` is ``[6, 7, 8, 9, 10]``.
    """
    _validate(total_items, per_page)
    if size < 1:
        raise ValueError("size must be at least 1")
    pages = page_count(total_items, per_page)
    if page < 1 or page > pages:
        raise ValueError("no such page")

    if pages <= size:
        return list(range(1, pages + 1))

    half = size // 2
    # With odd size, the current page is the middle of the window, so it
    # has ``half`` pages before it. With even size, the extra page goes
    # after the current page, so it has ``half - 1`` pages before it.
    before = half if size % 2 == 1 else half - 1
    first = page - before

    # Clamp so the window keeps its full length while staying in range.
    if first < 1:
        first = 1
    last = first + size - 1
    if last > pages:
        last = pages
        first = last - size + 1
    return list(range(first, last + 1))
